sketch.label: The team's whiteboard sketch
sketch.description: An informal sketch with eight boxes: Web app, Alert service, Poller, Registrar, SMS, Database, HTTP library, and Shared code. Unlabeled arrows run from Web app to Alert service, from Alert service to Poller and to SMS, from Database to Alert service, and from Poller to Registrar and to HTTP library. Plain lines join Shared code to Alert service and to Poller.
sketch.caption: An informal sketch, not UML: nothing says what a box or an arrow means.
sketch.source:
@startuml
layout horizontal
box "Web app" as web
box "Alert service" as svc
box "Poller" as poll
box "Registrar" as reg
box "SMS" as sms
box "Database" as db
box "HTTP library" as lib
box "Shared code" as shared
web --> svc
svc --> poll
poll --> reg
svc --> sms
db --> svc
poll --> lib
shared -- svc
shared -- poll
@enduml

parts.label: The seat-alert app's components
parts.description: Six components: StudentWeb, AlertService, SeatPoller, AlertDB, Registrar, and TextGateway. Notes say that Registrar is run by the university and TextGateway by an SMS company.
parts.caption: Each box is a component: a part that runs and can be replaced as a unit. The two notes mark the parts that other organizations run.
parts.source:
@startuml
layout square
component StudentWeb
component AlertService
component SeatPoller
component AlertDB
component Registrar
component TextGateway
note bottom of Registrar : run by the university
note bottom of TextGateway : run by an SMS company
@enduml

code_tree.label: The app's code view
code_tree.description: The seat-alert repository contains the folders web, service, poller, shared, and lib; lib contains http.
code_tree.caption: The code view shows how the source is organized. It is not a component diagram.
code_tree.source:
@startuml
seat-alert/
  web/
  service/
  poller/
  shared/
  lib/
    http/
@enduml

code_tree_mapped.label: The code view mapped to running components
code_tree_mapped.description: web runs as StudentWeb in 500 browsers; service runs as AlertService; poller runs as SeatPoller; shared is built into AlertService and SeatPoller; lib/http runs inside SeatPoller.
code_tree_mapped.caption: One folder can run as many copies, and one component can contain code from several folders.
code_tree_mapped.source:
@startuml
seat-alert/
  web/          # runs as StudentWeb in 500 browsers
  service/      # runs as AlertService
  poller/       # runs as SeatPoller
  shared/       # built into AlertService and SeatPoller
  lib/
    http/       # runs inside SeatPoller
@enduml

wiring.label: How AlertService is wired
wiring.description: AlertService's Watches ball sits in StudentWeb's socket. SeatPoller's news port connects to AlertService's events port through a «queue», and AlertService's store port connects to AlertDB's sql port over «SQL».
wiring.caption: Small squares on the edges are ports. Lines between ports are connectors labeled with their kind; the ball-and-socket assembly is an «HTTPS» request and reply.

overview.label: Dependency overview
overview.description: Dashed dependency arrows run from StudentWeb to AlertService; from AlertService to AlertDB, TextGateway, and SeatPoller; and from SeatPoller to Registrar.
overview.caption: A dashed arrow points from the component that needs to the component it needs.
overview.source:
@startuml
component StudentWeb
component AlertService
component SeatPoller
component AlertDB
component Registrar
component TextGateway
StudentWeb ..> AlertService
AlertService ..> AlertDB
AlertService ..> TextGateway
AlertService ..> SeatPoller
SeatPoller ..> Registrar
@enduml

full.label: The complete seat-alert component diagram
full.description: StudentWeb requires Watches, which AlertService provides. SeatPoller requires SeatCounts, which Registrar provides. AlertService requires TextMessages, which TextGateway provides. SeatPoller's news port connects to AlertService's events port through a «queue», and AlertService's store port connects to AlertDB over «SQL».
full.caption: Every ball-and-socket connector in this app is an «HTTPS» request and reply; the other connectors are labeled with their kind.

full_notes.label: The complete seat-alert component diagram
full_notes.description: StudentWeb requires Watches, which AlertService provides. SeatPoller requires SeatCounts, which Registrar provides. AlertService requires TextMessages, which TextGateway provides. SeatPoller's news port connects to AlertService's events port through a «queue», and AlertService's store port connects to AlertDB over «SQL». Notes say that Registrar is run by the university and TextGateway by an SMS company. A note serves as the key: a ball in a socket is an «HTTPS» call.
full_notes.caption: Every ball-and-socket connector in this app is an «HTTPS» request and reply; the other connectors are labeled with their kind.

push.label: AlertService with push notifications
push.description: AlertService and its partners. A new PushGateway provides PushMessages, and its ball sits in a new PushMessages socket on AlertService. StudentWeb still requires Watches, TextGateway still provides TextMessages, and AlertService's store port still connects to AlertDB over «SQL».
push.caption: The new PushGateway fills a new socket on AlertService; the other parts keep their interfaces.
